# The Workstation battery should fail on its own when a drag does not land where its preview showed

## Context

Operator, 2026-10-19, on #19866 (the v13.3 release blocker): the team ships flagship changes without detecting the bugs they bring. That ticket's two bugs were already in v13.2.0. Reverting the post-release dock commits changes neither, so they were never new; nobody found them:

- A tab-drag carried back over main painted an accepted preview, and the release put the pane in its popup.
- A second title-bar return was refused seven times by a stale park, then abandoned with no trace.

#19868 (a title-bar return right after another) belongs to the same class: a gesture the product previews or accepts ends somewhere else, and nothing says so.

## The Problem

The Workstation NL battery asserts the paths its authors drove: one return per session, and a morph arm that cancels rather than drops. A human repeats a gesture and releases where the preview shows. Nothing in the battery fails when either diverges. Hosted CI has run the tier since 2026-10-13 (`e2e-brain`, blocking, on every dev-based Engine PR in its impact boundary), and it passed with today's bugs in: no arm made the gestures.

## The Architectural Reality

- At release the engine holds both facts: the accepted preview (`DragAffordances`, `TabSortZone`, `DragCoordinator` candidates) and the commit or terminal it takes.
- The e2e gate `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs#workerErrors` already fails any test whose worker logs an error, so an engine-reported divergence turns every existing drag arm into a check without new assertions.
- Abandonment points that today end silently include the park refusal limit (`retryNativeWindowPark`) and the null-preview branch of `commitNativeWindowDrop` (#19868).

## The Fix (proposed)

1. **The engine reports a divergence.** A release whose accepted preview neither commits to that target nor ends in a reported refusal logs an error naming the preview, the terminal, and the item. Every abandoned gesture leaves a receipt.
2. **The battery repeats what a human repeats.** The flagship journey arms run each cross-window gesture twice in one session: return, pop out, return again.

Co-design conditions (Ada, owner of the NL tier in `#19655`, 2026-10-19), agreed:
- **Classify in the engine, never in the log text.** At release, an accepted preview ends in exactly one of four terminals: committed to its target, a reported refusal, a user cancel (Escape, walk-back), or abandoned/diverged. Only the last logs an error. A reported refusal is one the operator can see; anything else is an abandonment under another name.
- **One report per gesture, at its end.** A retried park reports once, at the abandonment, naming the preview, the terminal and the item, never once per retry.
- **The instrument has its own red.** Each abandonment point gets a unit arm proving it reports, because an arm that asserts "no error" passes once nothing reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With #19866's fixes reverted, the existing battery goes red through the reported divergence, without new assertions.
- [ ] Each abandonment point reports itself, once per gesture at its end, with a unit arm proving it reports; a cancel (Escape, a walk-back) and a reported refusal do not.
- [ ] The flagship journey arms repeat every cross-window gesture once.

## Out of Scope

- The specs hosted CI skips (`BRAIN_QUARANTINES` in `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`) and its retry bridge until 2026-10-25: #19655's closeout.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-19T16:32:32Z

**Design before code: the release terminals, where each is classified, and one hazard found while mapping.**

Intake (self-authored, stage 2): `Prescription checked: src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs + src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs — own the concern.` The per-gesture records already exist:
- `SortZone.activeTrace`: the pointer path, read by `get_drag_trace`, which already logs `end` and `cancel`.
- The native candidates plus `claimTrace`: the title-bar path, read by `get_drag_state`.

The classification lands beside their end resolution, through one `DragCoordinator` helper. It records `{path, itemId, preview, terminal, reason}` in a bounded ring that `get_drag_state` exposes, and it logs only the abandoned or diverged class, once per gesture. The stack drag's `dockStackDragTerminal` already classifies `committed | cancelled | rejected`; that is the precedent.

| # | Where | Accepted preview at release | Diverging terminal | Would have caught |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | the host's `dockTearOutTerminal` handler | this window's own in-window preview (`DragAffordances`, state `accepted`) | the tear-out committed instead | #19866 bug A |
| P2 | `DragAffordances#onDrop` | the rendered preview | nothing committed: generation or signature guard, null descriptor, reducer errors | a silently lost in-window drop |
| P3 | `DragCoordinator#retryNativeWindowPark` at its limit | the native hover preview whose dwell completed | the gesture ended | #19866 bug B, once, not per retry |
| P4 | `commitNativeWindowDrop`, null preview after its one wait | the same | the gesture ended | #19868 |
| P5 | `commitNativeWindowDrop`, embodiment settle failure or model refusal | the same | restored | a refusal no operator sees |

Not reported: a cancel (`dockCrossZoneDragCancel`, `dockTearOutCancel`, a walk-back), a remote commit, a release with no accepted preview, and a same-zone release the base reorder commits.

**Hazard.** Hover (`resolvePreview`) runs pointer inference over all of `geometry.zones`, but `onDrop` filters the source zone out of pointer inference, because the within-toolbar reorder owns same-zone drops. `PreviewProducer#produce` excludes nothing itself. A pointer-inferred preview over the source zone's body can therefore be painted and then never honored, which is the very class this ticket exists to surface. I'll measure it in the battery first. If any arm paints one, the fix is to align hover with drop (offer self-targets only through the indicator menu, as `onDrop`'s own comment intends), not to teach P2 to ignore it.

Unit arms: one per P-point proving it reports, plus "no report" arms for cancel and remote commit. Red-first is AC-1: revert #19866's fixes, and the existing battery goes red through P1/P3 with no new assertions.
